title: God of the Changing Year, Whose Arm of Power
description: God of the Changing Year, Whose Arm of Power in Tonic Solfa to SONG TWENTY-TWO, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Emily Taylor wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 400, “The Changing Year”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Tens (10.10.10.10), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SONG TWENTY-TWO; any other Tens tune fits them as well.
underlay: God of the chang-ing year, whose arm of power In safe-ty leads through dan-ger's dark-est hour, Here in Thy tem-ple bow Thy child-ren down, To bless Thy mer-cy, and Thy might to own.

lines: God of the changing year, whose arm of power
In safety leads through danger's darkest hour, —
Here in Thy temple bow Thy children down,
To bless Thy mercy, and Thy might to own.
Thine are the beams that cheer us on our way,
And pour around the gladdening light of day;
Thine is the night, and the fair orbs that shine
To cheer its hours of darkness, — all are Thine.
If round our path the thorns of sorrow grew,
And mortal friends were faithless, Thou wast true
Did sickness shake the frame, or anguish tear
The wounded spirit, Thou wast present there.
O, lend Thine ear, and lift our voice to Thee;
Where'er we dwell, still let Thy mercy be;
From year to year, still nearer to Thy shrine
Draw our frail hearts, and make them wholly Thine!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Emily Taylor died in 1872.
credits: Words by Emily Taylor (1795–1872), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to SONG TWENTY-TWO by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
